memory_annotations.evidence_summary: No durable preference evidence was expressed; all decisions were limited to the schedule and tradeoffs of this Chicago conference trip.

messages.content: I need to put together a Chicago trip for a university-press rights conference, Thursday, March 27 through Sunday, March 30. I have to be in the Denver office Thursday morning, so I cannot leave until after 10:00. The exhibitor briefing starts at 6:30 p.m. at the Chicago Marriott Downtown Magnificent Mile. My final session ends Sunday at 3:30 p.m. Can you compare flights and nearby hotels as complete packages?
Yes. Before I narrow it down, is this for 2025, and are you traveling alone? Also, what room and baggage assumptions should I use, and is there a target total for flight plus three hotel nights?
It is 2025 and just me. One carry-on, one room, either one king or one queen. Use about $1,500 total as the target, but show me a little above that if the schedule is materially better.

I found three workable outbound patterns. United has a nonstop from Denver at 11:35 a.m., arriving at O'Hare at 3:02 p.m., around $347 round trip with a Sunday evening return. American has a 12:20 p.m. nonstop arriving at O'Hare at 3:48 p.m., around $319. Southwest has a 12:05 p.m. nonstop arriving at Midway at 3:25 p.m., around $286. The United flight gives the strongest buffer for a 6:30 briefing. Near the venue, the Marriott itself is about $269 nightly, the Aloft Chicago Mag Mile is about $214, and the Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile is about $229. Those hotel rates are before tax.

The briefing is mandatory, so I do not want a plan that only works if everything goes perfectly. Please turn those into two or three complete combinations and include the likely airport-to-hotel timing.

Combination A is United to O'Hare plus the Marriott: depart Denver 11:35 a.m., land 3:02 p.m., and allow roughly 60 to 90 minutes by taxi or rideshare in weekday traffic. That should put you at the hotel around 4:15 to 4:45. Estimated trip total is $1,302 including airfare and hotel taxes. Combination B is United plus the Aloft: same flight and arrival buffer, an estimated total of $1,113, and about a seven-minute walk to the conference venue. Combination C is Southwest to Midway plus the Hilton Garden Inn: land at 3:25 p.m.; the drive is commonly 35 to 60 minutes, putting you at the hotel around 4:20 to 4:50. Estimated total is $1,086. All three leave meaningful time before 6:30, though the United options have about 20 minutes more schedule cushion.
Are all of those times local? And does the total include rides between the airport and hotel?

The departure time is Denver time and each Chicago arrival is Central time. The totals include round-trip airfare and three hotel nights with estimated lodging tax, but not airport transportation. For budgeting, I would add about $100 to $150 for two rideshare trips involving O'Hare, or about $80 to $120 involving Midway. Rail would cost much less but would take more handling time with luggage.
For this trip, remove the Midway option. I would rather use the extra arrival buffer than save the small difference.

That leaves two strong packages built around the 11:35 a.m. United nonstop to O'Hare. The Marriott package is the easiest operationally because the briefing is in the same building. The Aloft package saves about $189 after estimated tax and requires a short walk along East Ontario Street. With estimated rideshares included, the Marriott package is roughly $1,402 to $1,452, while the Aloft package is roughly $1,213 to $1,263.
What are the sensible Sunday return flights after a 3:30 finish? I will need enough time to collect my bag from the hotel and get to O'Hare.

The first return I would consider is United at 6:10 p.m., arriving Denver at 7:52 p.m. If you leave the venue by 3:40, collect your carry-on immediately, and depart for O'Hare around 4:00, it is workable but traffic could make it tense. The safer choice is United at 7:45 p.m., arriving Denver at 9:28 p.m. It gives nearly four hours from the session ending to departure and adds about $34 to the round-trip fare.
Please check the cancellation terms on both hotels and give me totals with the safer Sunday flight.

Using the 7:45 p.m. Sunday return, the United round trip is approximately $381. The Marriott's flexible rate is $279 per night and can be canceled without penalty until 11:59 p.m. two days before arrival; three nights with estimated tax come to about $973. Flight and hotel total: about $1,354. The Aloft's flexible rate is $224 per night with cancellation allowed until 6:00 p.m. two days before arrival; three nights with estimated tax come to about $781. Flight and hotel total: about $1,162. Adding a $125 midpoint estimate for O'Hare rides makes the planning totals about $1,479 and $1,287 respectively.
Does either rate include breakfast? Also, is the Aloft walk straightforward early in the morning and after conference dinners?

Neither quoted flexible rate includes breakfast. The Marriott has breakfast available on site, generally around $25 to $35 before gratuity. Aloft has a counter-service breakfast sold separately, and there are several cafes between the two hotels. The walk is roughly 0.3 mile on busy downtown streets, mostly along Ontario, and usually takes six to eight minutes. It is direct and well traveled, though late-night street conditions can vary as they do in any central business district.
The Aloft package seems like the sensible one. Before settling on it, can you compare the two Sunday flights more precisely, including when I would likely reach home in Denver?

With the 6:10 p.m. flight, you would land at 7:52 p.m. Mountain time. Allowing about 25 minutes to exit and 35 to 50 minutes for the ride from DEN, a reasonable home-arrival estimate is 8:55 to 9:15 p.m. That round trip is about $347. The 7:45 p.m. flight lands at 9:28 p.m., making the likely home arrival 10:30 to 10:50 p.m.; the round trip is about $381. The earlier flight saves $34 and gets you home around 95 minutes sooner, but you would want to leave the hotel for O'Hare no later than 4:00 p.m. The later flight is much more resilient to a session running over or heavy expressway traffic.

The final session is scheduled to end promptly, and I will only have the carry-on. Use the 6:10 return after all. Give me a concise recap of the best package and keep the Marriott as the backup. Do not book anything yet.

Best package: United nonstop outbound Thursday, March 27, departing DEN at 11:35 a.m. Mountain time and arriving ORD at 3:02 p.m. Central time; United nonstop return Sunday, March 30, departing ORD at 6:10 p.m. and arriving DEN at 7:52 p.m. Estimated round-trip airfare is $347. Stay three nights at Aloft Chicago Mag Mile, about a six- to eight-minute walk from the Chicago Marriott Downtown Magnificent Mile. The flexible room estimate is $224 nightly, approximately $781 including tax, with cancellation allowed until 6:00 p.m. two days before arrival. Flight and hotel total is about $1,128; with a $100 to $150 rideshare allowance, budget about $1,228 to $1,278. On Thursday, a typical rideshare should reach the hotel around 4:15 to 4:45 p.m., leaving time before the 6:30 briefing. On Sunday, collect the carry-on after the 3:30 session and leave for O'Hare by 4:00 p.m. Backup: the same flights with the conference Marriott at approximately $1,320 before airport transportation. No reservation has been made, and prices and inventory should be rechecked before purchase.

The conference Marriott remains the hotel backup. Nothing has been booked; fares, room inventory, cancellation deadlines, and final prices remain to be verified.
